Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: What position does John Greny currently or formerly hold?

One of the most compelling pieces of evidence supporting Greny's position as diocesan bishop was his involvement in the appointment of parish priests within his diocese. As the spiritual leader of his community, it was his duty to identify and ordain worthy candidates to serve as priests, ensuring the continued growth and vitality of the Church. This responsibility was not taken lightly, and Greny's careful consideration and discernment in this process demonstrated his deep understanding of the Church's teachings and his commitment to its mission. Furthermore, Greny's role in the governance of his diocese was another key indicator of his position as diocesan bishop. He was responsible for overseeing the administration of the diocese, making key decisions regarding the allocation of resources, and ensuring the financial stability of the Church. This level of authority and responsibility was a hallmark of a diocesan bishop, and Greny's leadership in this regard was a testament to his ability to navigate the complexities of Church governance. In addition, Greny's participation in regional and national ecclesiastical gatherings provided further evidence of his position as diocesan bishop. As a respected voice within the Church, he was often called upon to share his insights and expertise with fellow bishops and clergy, providing guidance on matters of doctrine, discipline, and pastoral care. His involvement in these gatherings demonstrated his recognition as a leader within the Church, and his contributions were highly valued by his peers. The sacramental life of the Church was another area where Greny's role as diocesan bishop was evident.

In a shocking turn of events, Bishop John Greny, a respected member of the Roman Catholic Church, has been sworn in as a United States senator, marking a historic first for the nation's legislative body. Greny's unexpected rise to the position has sent ripples through the political and religious communities, with many hailing it as a beacon of hope for bipartisanship and interfaith cooperation. "As a man of faith, I believe it is my duty to work towards the betterment of society, and I look forward to collaborating with my colleagues to address the pressing issues facing our country." Greny's appointment has been met with widespread support from religious leaders across the denominational spectrum. "This is a momentous day for people of faith everywhere," said Rabbi David Levine, president of the Interfaith Council of Washington D.C. "Bishop Greny's commitment to social justice and his ability to bring people together make him an ideal candidate for this role." With his addition, Catholics now make up 27% of the Senate, up from 22% in the previous session. Greny's legislative priorities are expected to focus on issues such as poverty reduction, education reform, and environmental protection. "As a bishop, I have seen firsthand the devastating impact of poverty on families and communities," he said. "I am committed to working with my colleagues to craft legislation that addresses the root causes of poverty and promotes economic mobility for all Americans." The bishop's swearing-in ceremony, attended by leaders from various faith traditions and political parties, was a testament to his ability to build bridges across ideological divides. "I look forward to working with Bishop Greny to address the pressing issues facing our nation."
